transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-17
Time: 16:00 - 16:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Jonah Ruiz (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Kestrel Lead ML Eng), Maya Lopez (Kestrel PM), Samir Rao (Kestrel Infra), Lina Chen (QA)

Summary (auto): Week three benchmark deltas vs baseline provider; median wins for Redwood in synthetic tests, tail latencies still above SLO under bursty patterns; suggested mitigations: prefix/KV caching, small increase in reserved concurrency, route-by-latency policy in canary.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um today's the week three sync for the POC, we ran the head-to-head against your incumbent last week and priya's going to walk through the results, i'll kick it over to her.
[00:18] Priya: thanks alex. hey team, um quick note - i have the slide deck and the raw bench logs in the shared folder, link in chat, but i'll summarize the key deltas: median latency improved by ~12% across our quantized v2 profile at 512 tokens, throughput (tokens/sec) is similar to the incumbent at steady state, but 95th and 99th percentiles show a tail under burst that is about 20-30% higher on our cluster for short sequences.
[00:45] Maya: can you clarify "quantized v2 profile" — is that per your automated recommend engine or a manual setting? looks like the deck calls it qv2.
[00:55] Priya: yeah it's the automated suggest from Redwood Optimize — it's a 4-bit symmetric quant run with KV-cache friendly kernels. small note: sometimes the transcriber shows kv cash, ignore that :)
[01:05] Daniel: quick question on the test harness - did you replay our production request distribution or a synthetic Poisson load? that will affect tail behaviour.
[01:15] Jonah: good point. for this run we replayed your supplied distribution file for weekday daytime traffic but with an injected 10% burst every five minutes to stress tail. we documented it in the logs CSV.
[01:28] Samir: when you say injected burst, are we talking concurrent request spikes or tokens-per-second spikes? we saw a big jump in concurrency on our side previously.
[01:38] Priya: concurrent spike - we ramped concurrency from baseline by 3x for 30 seconds in the burst window.
[01:44] Lina: and the baseline tests — were they run on the same instance types? your notes said "mismatch in hardware vram" earlier.
[01:52] Priya: yes, thanks for flagging. baseline (IncumbentAI) used c-type A100 equivalents; our Redwood hosted cluster used a mixed pool: mostly A800 equivalents but a small subset hit an older A30-equivalent node during bursts due to autoscale timing. that caused some outlier tokens. we flagged that to infra for immediate remediation.
[02:12] Daniel: okay that could explain tail — we can repro if you give the exact node list and times.
[02:18] Alex: yeah we'll share the raw node-level logs and the timestamped traces, that's part of the next steps.
[02:24] Maya: can you walk through the specific numbers — median, p95, p99 for both providers at 512 tokens?
[02:32] Priya: sure. i'll read the numbers, these are medians across 30 minute windows: Redwood median 82ms, Incumbent median 94ms. Redwood p95 240ms, Incumbent p95 190ms. Redwood p99 480ms, Incumbent p99 410ms. throughput tokens/sec (steady-state) Redwood 12.4k tps, Incumbent 12.1k tps.
[03:02] Daniel: got it — median looks nice but those p95 numbers are concerning. what's the confidence interval?
[03:09] Priya: 95% CI for p95 is roughly +/- 12ms; we ran three repeats and the delta is consistent.
[03:16] Jonah: another nuance - we saw the tail correlate with cold-KV-cache misses on prefix-heavy prompts, when the KV cache wasn't warmed it falls back to full attention and that's what's spiking the p95.
[03:29] Samir: is that a model architecture thing or runtime / pipeline ordering?
[03:33] Priya: mostly runtime — our serving runtime supports prefix/KV caching but with the mixed instance pool some checkpoints didn't persist across the autoscale boundary; we think dedicated slots or sticky routing would reduce that.
[03:44] Daniel: can you test with sticky sessions? that's similar to what we do on the incumbent.
[03:49] Priya: yes we can run a follow-up with prefix sticky routing. we'll also enable a caching warm-up phase before cutover windows.
[03:55] Maya: what's the estimated improvement if you enable sticky routing?
[03:58] Priya: based on traces we estimate p95 could drop from 240ms to ~170-180ms in burst windows — closer to incumbent. median stays similar.
[04:07] Lina: any changes to token cost with sticky routing / caching?
[04:12] Alex: caching reduces tokens processed for repeated prefixes so unit cost drops slightly; in synthetic the cost delta was ~6% lower with caching.
[04:18] Daniel: you mentioned quantization artifacts earlier — did you observe quality diffs vs incumbent on Rouge / perplexity?
[04:25] Priya: for the qv2 profile at 4-bit, we saw negligible generation differences on your internal eval set for prompts <600 tokens. for longer sequences some subtle repetition patterns emerged in 2 out of 2000 samples — we captured those in the artifact report.
[04:39] Maya: we need that artifact report — those edge cases matter for our compliance team.
[04:44] Priya: yes we'll share the artifacts and the sample IDs.
[04:48] Jonah: also worth noting the Incumbent ran mostly FP16 so their p95 looks better because they didn't hit autoscale boundaries as often. our plan is to align instance homogeneity for the next run or reserve dedicated slots to remove autoscale variance.
[05:03] Samir: what would dedicated look like for our trial? can you give a rough cost delta?
[05:09] Alex: ballpark — for a small dedicated pool to match your peak concurrency we estimated roughly 25% higher monthly committed cost vs our bursty hosted tier but you'd get predictable tail and no autoscale crossing. i'll send a formal quote.
[05:19] Daniel: prefer quote in same spreadsheet as benchmarks so we can share with finance.
[05:23] Alex: noted.
[05:25] [06:00] Priya: jumping forward — throughput story is good: tokens/sec matches incumbent at steady state; when we hit the burst we see small drop because background GC and kernel handoffs on mixed nodes cause edge serialization. we have a runtime patch to reduce handoffs which we'll apply in the next lab run.
[06:18] Daniel: runtime patch — is that disruptive? do you need a model restart?
[06:22] Priya: non-disruptive, it's a kernel scheduling tweak. we'll roll to canary then prod in lab.
[06:28] Maya: procurement question — is there an SLA we can point to if we go dedicated? also SOC2?
[06:34] Alex: dedicated comes with an uptime SLA, and we have SOC2 Type II and ISO docs — i'll drop the security pack link after the call.
[06:40] Samir: what's in the audit logs? we need token-level tracing and redaction controls.
[06:45] Jonah: we support token-level cost/latency breakdowns and per-request metadata; logs can be routed to your S3 or SIEM, and we support KMS for encryption at rest. redaction is configurable.
[06:58] Daniel: do you support bringing your private control plane (VPC) for this POC? we need to test private deployment later this quarter.
[07:06] Alex: yes Private (VPC) is on our roadmap for the pilot phase — we can outline the steps, network requirements, and timeline in a separate doc.
[07:12] Maya: back to the bench: can you share the raw latencies with per-region breakdowns? we saw some east-coast nodes with higher tail.
[07:20] Priya: yes raw node-level logs and region tags will be attached to the bench sheet.
[07:25] Lina: for QA i want to run our synthetic suite on the Redwood quant variant overnight — can we run an extra job with your qv2 + prefix cache enabled?
[07:34] Priya: absolutely — we'll queue an overnight run with caching and sticky sessions enabled. expect results next day.
[07:40] Daniel: one more technical question — do you support dynamic routing by latency SLO so we can fallback to incumbent if our p95 breaches?
[07:48] Jonah: yes that's supported via our routing policies: route-by-latency, cost, or region. you can set an automatic fallback to a vetted incumbent model variant. that would incur cross-provider calls though — need to evaluate cost.
[08:00] Maya: can you show a quick example of routing policy JSON?
[08:04] Jonah: i'll paste a sample in chat after this, but essentially it's a rule: if p95 > X for 5 minutes, shift Y% traffic to fallback.
[08:12] Samir: latency to fallback might add complexity; are we able to do async reroute for non-SLA paths?
[08:18] Priya: yes you can do partial reroutes for low priority routes, or do per-request flags for tolerant calls.
[08:24] Daniel: what's the effort to run the 10k sample you mentioned earlier? how long?
[08:28] Priya: 10k requests across your distribution will take about 2 hours with warm-up; we'll enable sticky and caching and share traces. we'll also run a control without caching for comparison.
[08:36] Maya: great. timeline?
[08:38] Priya: we can start tonight and have results by Monday 2026-04-20.
[08:43] Alex: putting that as a next step — priya to run, daniel to validate distribution file, alex to send quote and security pack.
[08:51] Lina: small note — on the last run we saw a transcription mismatch in the logs where some request IDs were truncated; please ensure request-id propagation is intact.
[08:59] Jonah: good catch — we'll add stronger request-id tagging and include it in the logs.
[09:06] Daniel: on cost — you said caching reduces token cost by ~6% in synthetic; what's the expected real-world delta?
[09:12] Alex: depends on prefix reuse, but we saw 4-10% cost savings on customer workloads with moderate prefix reuse. we can model cost per 1M tokens and show a sensitivity table.
[09:23] Maya: ok please include a sensitivity table in the spreadsheet.
[09:28] Priya: noted.
[09:30] [40:00] Alex: any blockers from the Kestrel side for us to run the sticky/cached job tonight?
[09:35] Daniel: we just need you to use the updated distribution CSV (version v3) — i'll upload it to the shared folder in five mins.
[09:41] Alex: perfect.
[09:43] Maya: last thing — procurement asked if we could get a short T&Cs summary and an example MSA.
[09:48] Alex: i'll loop in legal and share a redacted MSA template and T&C one-pager.
[09:53] Samir: thanks.
[09:55] Priya: ok i'll run the overnight with sticky routing and caching, and attach raw traces + the artifact report for quantization.
[09:59] Alex: great — recap of action items in chat, thanks everyone.

Auto-generated action items (end of call):
- Priya: run 10k sample with prefix caching + sticky routing, share raw traces and p95/p99 breakdown (due 2026-04-19)
